info.title: Blackwall internal API
info.description: The web app's own API. It may change without notice; integrations should use /api/v1 (see /api/v1/openapi.json). Workspace-scoped work management. Commands require versions of affected entities. Authenticate with Authorization: Bearer <token> or the HttpOnly session cookie plus X-CSRF-Token for mutations.

get.description: Streams the always-loaded records from one snapshot. A header carries cursor, last_mutation_id and schema; a trailer confirms the record count. Accept-Encoding negotiates gzip. A user runs one bootstrap at a time; others get 503 with Retry-After.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: User the replica belongs to. A different account is 401 `account changed`.

get.description: Server-sent pokes for workspace commits. Sends one poke on connect and one per commit, coalesced to one per 250 ms with keep-alive comments every 15 seconds. A poke's data is {"txid": n, "epoch": "..."}, the highest committing transaction it stands for and the epoch of the history that transaction belongs to, or {} when the client cannot tell what changed and must pull. A client may skip the pull only when the epoch equals its cursor's epoch, its cursor's xip is empty and txid is below its cursor's xmax. Each stream ends after 30 minutes; clients reconnect.

post.description: Applies one client's ordered mutations through the same store code as the command endpoint. Each mutation runs in its own transaction; business errors reject that mutation while transient failures stop the batch. A client row whose high-water mark is below the request's `acknowledged` id means the server lost the client's state: the batch is refused with 409 `client state lost` and nothing is applied.

changes.description:
Values before and after, for the `fields` that have them. Empty on rows written before
values were stored.

fields.description: Issue fields an update changed, so the timeline can say what moved.

prefix.description: The secret's first characters, for recognizing a token without revealing it.

workspace_ids.description: Null allows every workspace the user belongs to.

email_verification.description: Whether unverified accounts must verify their email address before signing in.

Change.description: One changed record in the requested REST or sync shape, or null when deleted or invisible.

entity.description: `workspace`, `members`, `issues`, or a workspace collection name such as `teams`.

default_stage_ids.description:
Client-chosen ids for the default stages, in stage order
(Backlog, Todo, In progress, Done). Absent means the server
generates them.

key.description: Prefixes the team's issue numbers, as in `ENG-42`. Unique in the workspace.

archive_after_days.description: Days after Done before auto-archive. Null means never.

oneOf.description:
Renames the team and changes its key. Issue keys under a former key keep
resolving, and no other team can take a key this team has used.

Deletes the team with its stages, sprints and memberships. Refused while
it holds any issue, archived and trashed ones included.
Removes the label from every issue, trashed ones included.
Sets who leads the project, where it stands and when it runs.
Deletes the project's milestones too and clears both from its issues.

user_id.description: The member whose subscription changes. Absent means the actor.

oneOf.description: Renames the workspace and changes the slug in its app URLs.
Members may remove themselves unless they are the workspace's only owner.
Makes `user_id` an owner and the acting owner an admin.

created_at.description:
The `created_at` the reader saw. A later change keeps the notification unread.
Clients older than coalesced change notifications omit it and read it regardless.

notifications.description:
The unread notifications the reader saw. Others, and any changed since, stay unread.
Clients older than coalesced change notifications omit it and read every one.

email_assignment.description:
Clients from before email notifications omit the email choices, which keeps the
stored ones.

events.description: Public webhook event types. Empty means every event.

include_data.description: Deliveries carry the changed record as `data`. Defaults to true.

events.description: Replaces the subscribed event types when present.

oneOf.description: Set by `invite` and `resend_invitation`. Idempotent replays leave it out.
Set on comments sent to or imported from an issue tracker.
The token that wrote the comment for its author, if one did.

CommentTracker.description: The remote comment a local comment corresponds to.

author_name.description: The remote author's name when no member maps to them; None for sent comments.

expires_in_days.description: Days until expiry, 1 to 366. Omit for a token that never expires.

workspace_ids.description: Restrict the token to these workspaces. Omit to allow all of the user's workspaces.

slug.description: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 48 bytes.

secret.description: Shown once. Only its hash is stored.

FieldChange.description:
One field an issue update changed. References hold ids, so a later rename shows the new
name. The description and dependencies carry no values: the text can be large, and
consecutive description edits share one activity row.

values.description:
Strings or null. Null stands for an empty field, or an empty set for `labels` and
`dependencies`.

FormerKey.description: A team and number an issue held before it moved to another team. Its key still names the issue.

events.description: Public webhook event types to deliver. Empty means every event.

include_data.description: Whether deliveries carry the changed record as `data`.

InvitationProof.description: A pending invitation to the registering address, as in an invitation link.

created_by.description: None for synced issues without a mapped author and for issues logged before creators were stored.

after.description: Continue an ungrouped Updated page using its next_cursor. Requires offset=0.

projection.description: Summary omits description and detail-only relations. Full is the offline sync shape.

where.description: Clauses ANDed together; see docs/filters.md. In a query string, the JSON array as text.

oneOf.description:
Moves the issue to another team under that team's next number. Its old key keeps
resolving. Without `stage_id` it lands in the team's first stage of the same kind. It
leaves its sprint, and its project when the project doesn't include the team.

IssuedInvitation.description: The only copy of a new invitation token. The database keeps its hash.

emailed.description: False when this server has no mail configured, so the admin must share the link.

LabelChange.description:
A list replaces every label. `{add, remove}` changes only the labels it names, and a
label in both is removed. Servers from before `{add, remove}` reject it as a type error
instead of acknowledging an edit they can't apply.

changes.description:
Every record the operation changed that the caller can see, including side effects such
as a parent's subtask counts. A null record was deleted or is no longer visible.

PendingLogin.description: A correct password on an account with TOTP. Finish signing in with a code.

cursor.description:
Opaque cursor, `epoch@` and a snapshot in `xmin:xmax:xip` text form.
Every txid below the snapshot's xmax except those listed is reflected.
An unfinished page may append `:txid.row`, the one transaction
delivered only up to that change row.

last_mutation_id.description:
The client's high-water mark on a final page. Null on intermediate
pages so the outbox is dropped only once all effects have arrived,
and null on resets and cursorless responses, which must not
acknowledge the outbox.

more.description: True when more pages remain. `last_mutation_id` is null then.

reset.description: True when the client must bootstrap again.

acknowledged.description:
The highest mutation id the client has seen acknowledged by a pull or bootstrap.
A stored high-water mark below it means the server lost the client's state, so
the batch is refused with 409 instead of re-running mutations. Defaults to 0.

RecoveryCodes.description: Shown once. The server keeps only their hashes.

RegistrationMode.description: Who may create an account, from `REGISTRATION` at startup.

Resource.description: A kind of record a workspace can hold only so many of.

SessionInfo.description: A signed-in browser or client, as security settings list it.

number.description: Counts up per team. The store assigns it on insert, so imported values are ignored.

SyncMutation.description:
One client mutation. `name` plus `args` form a `Command`; `at` is the
client's timestamp, validated but otherwise unused by the server.

archive_after_days.description: Days after entering Done before auto-archive. Null means never.

former_keys.description:
Keys the team had before, sorted. Issue keys under them keep resolving,
and no other team can take them.

key.description:
Prefixes the team's issue numbers, as in `ENG-42`. Unique in the workspace.
Transfers without one get a key derived from the name.

code.description: A six-digit code from the authenticator app, or a recovery code.
A six-digit code from the authenticator app.
A six-digit code from the authenticator app, or a recovery code.

qr_svg.description: `uri` as a QR code in an SVG document.

secret.description: The shared secret in base32, for typing into an authenticator app.

TrackerLink.description: Links an issue to the remote item it was imported from.

push_error.description: Last failed outbound push, cleared on success.

status_name.description: Last seen remote status name, for display.

Usage.description: How many of one resource a workspace holds, against its limit.

limit.description: None when the resource is unlimited.

Via.description:
The personal access token a write went through. The actor is still the token's user;
this says an integration or agent acted for them.

name.description: The token's name when it acted, such as `Claude Code`.

slug.description: Names the workspace in app URLs. Unique across the server.
